$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: stripCriterionAnnotation's own docstring names two shapes a single trailing-group
regex cannot strip, and neither had a fixture. A chained decoration (`MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery) (revised)`)
defeats a regex matching only the last `(...)`, leaving the first group in the stripped result. A nested one
(`Disaster Recovery (evaluated separately (see appendix))`) is worse: a regex excluding parens from its own
captured content (`[^()]*`) cannot describe a group containing another group at all, so the whole annotation is
left unstripped. Three review passes on Story 8.1's second commit flagged the chained case as untested; the
nested case was found independently, reproduced directly against stripCriterionAnnotation before this fixture was
The report is CONSTRUCTED: gapped-correct-audit's report with MTTR's heading chained
(`### MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery) (revised)`) and Disaster Recovery's heading nested
(`### Disaster Recovery (evaluated separately (see appendix))`), and nothing else touched.
stripCriterionAnnotation now peels balanced trailing parenthetical groups one at a time by counting parens from
the end, rather than matching them with a single regex, so both shapes strip to their bare ground-truth names.
Reverting to the single-group regex and replaying this case fails it: groundedCriteria moves from {17,17} to
{15,15}, losing MTTR and Disaster Recovery, the two criteria this case decorated, which is the regression this
derivation: Two headings gained parenthetical decoration, one chained and one nested, and nothing else changed, so every
status, count and ceiling below is gapped-correct-audit's own.
Statuses, coverage, thresholds, overall, unknownThreshold and cleanFalsePositives: identical to gapped-correct-audit,
since none of those readers are sensitive to a criterion heading's decoration.
Citations: identical set, order and count to gapped-correct-audit; neither heading's Evidence line changed.
Grounding: seventeen of the seventeen criteria with declared evidence are grounded, matching gapped-correct-audit
exactly. `MTTR (Mean Time To Recovery) (revised)` peels to `MTTR` and `Disaster Recovery (evaluated separately
(see appendix))` peels to `Disaster Recovery`, one balanced trailing group at a time; both resolve to their
ground-truth names and both still cite `evidence/reliability-2026-08.json`. ungroundedCitations stays empty.
